5 تختّم , or تختّم خَاتَمًا, (accord. to different copies of the S,) or تختّم بِخَاتَمٍ, (K, [agreeably with a trad. cited in the TA,]) He put on [i. e. put on his own finger] a خاتم [or signet-ring]. (S, K.) ―
-b2- And تختّم (tropical:) He put on a turban: (K, TA:) or تختّم بِعِمَامَتِهِ he put on his turban in the manner of a نِقَاب [q. v.]; syn. تَنَقَّبَ بِهَا. (Z, TA.) The subst. [signifying the act or mode, of doing so] is ↓ تَخْتِمَةٌ [q. v. infrà]. (K.) ―
-b3- تختّم بِأَمْرِهِ (assumed tropical:) He concealed his affair, or case. (Z, K.) ―
-b4- تختّم عَنْهُ (tropical:) He feigned himself heedless of him, and was silent [to him]. (K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
